terms.definition: A number that divides another number evenly, or multiplies with a partner to equal it.
terms.function: 4 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 4 = 3 with no remainder.
terms.whereItIs: Each number shown on the factor-pair cards.
terms.whyItMatters: Factors are the building blocks of a number's structure.

terms.definition: Two factors that multiply together to produce the number.
terms.function: 3 × 4 = 12, so (3, 4) is a factor pair of 12.
terms.whereItIs: The multiplication cards arranged around the center number.
terms.whyItMatters: Factor pairs make it efficient to list all factors of a number.

terms.definition: The property of a number being divisible by another with no remainder.
terms.function: Confirms whether a candidate is a factor — even division means yes.
terms.whereItIs: The division proof flipped up on each factor card.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the test that decides which numbers count as factors.

terms.definition: The complete set of numbers that divide a number evenly.
terms.function: Shows every factor, from 1 up to the number itself.
terms.whereItIs: The front list plate showing 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 for 12.
terms.whyItMatters: Listing factors is the first step of prime factorization and simplifying fractions.

terms.definition: A whole number with more than two factors.
terms.function: 12 has six factors, so it is composite.
terms.whereItIs: The center card when it shows 12, 18, or 24.
terms.whyItMatters: Composite numbers can be broken into factor pairs; primes cannot.
